details.body: Several NO3 envelope bounds in medium_planted and warm_room scenarios are extremely narrow — e.g., (4.0, 5.5), (4.5, 5.5), (4.5, 6.0) — representing only 1–1.5 mg N/L of range. These track the source water nitrate concentration (moderate.toml: 5.0 mg N/L) rather than meaningful biological behavior. Downstream beads (tanksim-6e5.2.3, 2.4, 2.5) will normalize nitrogen-cycle kinetics and plant uptake, which will shift NO3 dynamics. Widen these bounds to at least ±2–3 mg/L (e.g., (2.0, 8.0)) so they catch real regressions without breaking on every parameter tune. Document that NO3 bounds for moderate/warm_room scenarios include a source-water contribution of ~5 mg N/L.

Envelope::check silently passes NaN values in all f64 fields (pH, DO, TAN, NO2, NO3, reproductive_readiness, plant_biomass, algae_nuisance, biofilter_maturity, periphyton_biomass, fast_stem_biomass) because NaN comparisons return false in IEEE 754. Add a NaN/Inf guard at the top of the check method: for every constrained f64 field, if the snapshot value is not finite, push a violation like 'pH is NaN (expected [{min}, {max}])'. The existing final_finite assertions only catch NaN at the end of multi-hour runs, not at intermediate checkpoints where the root cause would be easier to diagnose.

The maintained_medium_variant_reaches_reproduction_window test zeroes out both shrimp_base_mortality_per_day and shrimp_stress_mortality_scale, forces periphyton biomass to ≥5g, forces adult reserve to ≥3g, forces reproductive_readiness to ≥0.5, and extends maturation to 120 days. This amount of state manipulation means the test doesn't protect the natural reproduction pathway — it only proves reproduction can happen under artificially perfect conditions. Add a doc comment explicitly stating this is a 'controlled ideal' test (not a naturalistic baseline), and consider adding a companion test with at most mortality zeroed (no other manipulations) to verify that at least adult survival is achievable under maintained-tank conditions without rigging reserves and readiness.

`enforce_invariants` now repairs shrimp egg bookkeeping on every simulation step by calling `reconcile_egg_cohort_counts()` (`crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:42-48`; `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:789-794`). When `berried_females_count` is larger than the cohort sum, that helper fabricates a new `EggCohort` at the current `egg_progress_days` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:600-620`), and the new validation test explicitly blesses that behavior (`crates/tank_core/tests/validation.rs:263-300`). This means a transient bookkeeping bug or partially migrated state can silently create near-hatching clutches instead of surfacing an invariant violation, which changes live simulation outcomes and can duplicate births. Please keep this kind of repair at load/migration boundaries only, or fail runtime invariant enforcement on mismatches instead of synthesizing eggs.

The new e2e suite introduces multiple `medium_planted` runs with the same seed (`crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:245-247`, `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:778-780`, `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:833-860`), but `HarnessRun::artifact_dir()` keys failure artifacts only by `scenario_id` and seed (`crates/tank_harness/src/lib.rs:546-553`). In a failing or parallel run, those tests all write to the same `/tmp/tank_harness/medium_planted_seed42` directory and can overwrite each other’s `trace.jsonl`, ledger, and metadata. Because `from_state()` still records the maintained variant as plain `medium_planted` (`crates/tank_harness/src/lib.rs:408-419`), the surviving artifact is also ambiguous. Give each harness run an explicit artifact/test label and include it in the artifact path/metadata.

`maintained_medium_variant_reaches_reproduction_window` is presented as a reproduction guardrail, but it is not actually baselining current scenario behavior: it manually boosts periphyton, adult reserve, and reproductive readiness, then disables shrimp mortality entirely (`crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:849-858`). That means the test can still pass after regressions in the real survival/stress model, because adults are prevented from dying and start with artificial hidden-state headroom. If reproduction needs its own envelope, it should be a named scenario/fixture built from public startup parameters with normal mortality semantics left on.
